Ghiyasuddin died at this time in 1325 AD.
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq also destroyed the 'Jwalamukhi Temple' of Kangra. He was known for his religious fanaticism and destroyed temples and confiscated their libraries for Persian translations.

question: What was the main function of 'Diwan-e-Bandagi' department and how many people were there in it?
solution: Firoz Shah's slaves were taught to work in factories. After the death of the Sultan, these slaves interfered in politics and played a role in the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty.

question: Who defeated Mohammad Ghori in the 'Battle of Anilwada' in 1178 AD?
solution: This was Mohammad Ghori's first major defeat in India. After this defeat, Ghori changed his route and planned to enter India through Punjab.

question: Who was the head of 'Diwan-e-Wizarat'?
solution: The Tughlaq period is called the 'Golden Age of Wazirat', because at this time the Wazirs had the maximum powers. During the time of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, the post of Wazir was very respected.

question: Which temple of South India was looted by 'Malik Kafur' and he obtained immense gold?
options: Meenakshi Temple and Chidambaram Temple of Madurai
solution: Taking advantage of the mutual feud between the Pandya kings (Veera Pandya and Sundara Pandya), Malik Kafur reached Madurai. He was the first general of the Delhi Sultanate who campaigned near Kanyakumari.

question: 'Qutub Minar' was named in honor of which famous person?
options: In the name of Caliph Qutub
solution: Near Qutub Minar is the Dargah of Khwaja Bakhtiyar Kaki. Aibak was his great follower. Quranic verses and praises of saints are written on the walls of the minaret.

question: What was 'Biswa' at the time of Alauddin?
options: A type of tax was Kharaj.
solution: Alauddin Khilji made Biswa the standard unit to prevent revenue theft. He abolished the rights of middlemen (Khoot and Muqaddam) so that farmers could pay taxes directly to the state.

question: In which year was Ibrahim Lodi, the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, defeated?
solution: The main reasons for Ibrahim Lodi's defeat were the rebellion of his chieftains and Babur's modern artillery. With this a big chapter of medieval history in India ended.

question: Which class did Razia Sultan displease the most during her reign?
options: Ottoman nobles and the Chalisa party
solution: Razia also had the title of 'Umdat-ul-Niswan' (the greatest among women) inscribed on her coins. His fall was the result of court conspiracies.

question: Which Sultan abolished the department of 'Diwan-e-Insha' and created 'Diwan-e-Mustakharaj'?
solution: Alauddin Khilji's administrative system was entirely focused on control and revenue generation. He took back the gifted lands (Milk and Waqf).

question: During whose reign did Genghis Khan (Mongol) pose a threat of invasion to India's borders?
solution: In 1221 AD, Genghis Khan reached the border of India. Iltutmish refused to give shelter to Jalaluddin, due to which Genghis Khan returned satisfied and Delhi was saved from the havoc of the Mongols.

question: Where did Alauddin Khilji order to store grains under his 'market control' policy?
options: He created a store of grains in government warehouses in Delhi for rationing during famine.
solution: Alauddin started the 'famine relief' system. During times of famine, a certain quantity (about half a maund) of grain was given to each household every day.

question: Out of the five floors of 'Qutub Minar', the top two floors are made of which stone?
solution: The fourth and fifth floors of the minar are the gift of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. After this, Sikandar Lodi also got the upper part repaired, due to which architecture of different periods is visible in it.

question: How did Babar decorate the cannons during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi?
options: On the walls of the fort.
solution: This technique of Babar confused Ibrahim's huge army. When the Rajputs and Afghans attacked, they came directly in front of the cannons, causing massive destruction.

question: What was the post of 'Amir-e-Tuzuk' during the Sultanate period?
solution: The names of posts in the Sultanate administration were based on Persian and Turkish traditions. The power of the Sultan depended on the loyalty of these officers.

question: Who was 'Munni' (Munhiyan) during the Sultanate period?
solution: Alauddin Khilji had spread such a network of Munni and Barid (official spies) that the nobles were afraid to talk to each other even in their homes.

question: When did 'Tarmashreen' attack India during the time of Mohammad Bin Tughlaq?
solution: Bribing the Mongols was another controversial policy of the MBT. This boosted the morale of the Mongols and emptied the Sultanate's treasury.

question: What type of coins did 'Bahlol Lodi' mint during his reign?
solution: Bahlol Lodi tried to stabilize the economy. The value of his coin was equal to 1/4 tanka. He promoted Afghan trade.

question: In which year did 'Lahore' fall during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi?
solution: The victory of Lahore was very important for Babur. He camped his army there and planned the final attack on Delhi.

question: What was the function of the 'Diwan-e-Ishtiaq' department created by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
options: Giving donations for the marriage of girls
To administer justice: For this there was 'Diwan-e-Qaza'.
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq introduced the concept of public welfare state. He prepared a list of unemployed people and gave them government jobs as per their qualifications.

question: 'Barid-e-Mumalik' was the highest official of which department during the Sultanate period?
solution: Barid-e-Mumalik had to be very confidant of the Sultan. Often he dined with the Sultan so that no one could poison him.

question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi Sultanate who first imposed 'Irrigation Tax'?
solution: Irrigation tax was called 'Haq-e-Sharb'. Firoz Shah collected this tax in return for the maintenance of canals and irrigation facilities, which increased the income of the state.

question: Who completed the construction work of Qutub Minar?
solution: Qutub Minar was named in honor of the famous Sufi saint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki. It is the tallest stone minaret in India and is an example of Indo-Islamic architecture.

question: Which was the dynasty of Delhi Sultanate which uprooted the 'Syed' dynasty?
solution: The fall of the Syed dynasty was very quiet. The last ruler Alam Shah went to Badaun and happily handed over his power to Bahlol Lodi.

question: What was the official language of the court during the reign of the Turks?
solution: The Persian language developed greatly during the Delhi Sultanate. Poets like Amir Khusro wrote their works in this language. It remained the administrative language of India until the end of the Mughal period.

question: Which last attempt was made by Alauddin Khilji to get 'Queen Padmini' after conquering 'Chittor'?
options: He had tried to immolate himself in the fire after performing Jauhar in the fort.
He made a treaty with them.
solution: According to history and folklore, Alauddin could never see Queen Padmini alive. The conquest of Chittor proved to be a 'hollow victory' for him.

question: In which language has the epic 'Prithviraj Raso' been composed?
solution: Prithviraj Raso is considered to be the first epic of Hindi. It describes the love story of Prithviraj Chauhan and Princess Sanyogita and the battles of Tarain.

question: Who was the ruler of Delhi Sultanate who introduced the 'Iqta System' and 'Turkan-e-Chihalgani' (Chalisa)?
solution: Iltutmish also introduced coins called 'Tanka' of silver and 'Jital' of copper. He made Delhi the capital of the Sultanate and received 'Mansoor' (charter of authority) from the Caliph.

question: Whom did Bahlol Lodi defeat the Sharqi Sultans of 'Jaunpur' and make him the governor there?
options: Sikandar Lodi was the successor of Sikandar Sultan.
solution: Barbak Shah later rebelled against his brother Sikandar Lodi, which Sikandar successfully suppressed and completely annexed Jaunpur to Delhi.

question: Which secret department was created by Alauddin Khilji after banning 'liquor and gambling'?
solution: Alauddin believed that conspiracies for rebellion were born from social interaction. His spies were so active that, according to Barani, "the Sultan was even aware of the food cooked in the houses of the nobles."

question: What was the religious reason given by 'Taimur Lang' for attacking India?
options: Destroying the 'infidels' of India and spreading Islam
solution: Taimur has written in his memoir 'Tuzuk-e-Taimuri' that he came to India to destroy idols and for the victory of Islam. He named his attack 'Jihad'.

question: Which dress did Razia Sultan abandon the practice of purdah and start sitting in the court?
solution: This behavior of Razia greatly irritated the Turkish nobles. They considered it against Islam and against the dignity of women, which became a reason for Razia's downfall.

question: Bahlol Lodi defeated which ruler of Jaunpur and reunited it with the Delhi Sultanate?
solution: The conquest of Jaunpur was very important for Bahlol Lodi as it re-established the prestige of Delhi. Bahlol appointed his son Barbak Shah as the governor of Jaunpur.

question: When did Firoz Shah Tughlaq introduce 'Jizya' as a separate tax?
options: After establishing the city of Jaunpur, it had no direct connection with Jaziya.
When he imposed it on Brahmins also
After the Bengal conquest, he gave tax exemption to Muslims during the Bengal campaign.
When he became Sultan, he initially allowed the old taxes to continue.
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first Sultan who imposed Jaziya even on Brahmins. When the Brahmins of Delhi went on a hunger strike in protest, the Hindus of Delhi decided to pay their share of Jizya themselves.

question: What was the main function of 'Diwan-e-Rasalat' department?
options: Management of Religious Affairs and Grants
solution: 'Sadr-us-sudoor' was the head of this department. He was responsible for enforcing the religious laws of the state and overseeing Islamic endowments (Waqf).

question: Which step was taken by Balban to strengthen his army under the policy of 'blood and iron'?
options: He kept only loyal Turkish soldiers in the army.
Gave high military posts to Hindus
solution: 'Imad-ul-Mulk' was the Diwan-i-Arz (military minister) during the time of Balban, who restored discipline in the army with the help of the Sultan. Balban introduced the practice of conducting periodic parades and inspections of the troops.

question: Between whom was the first battle of Panipat (1526 AD) fought?
solution: Babar used 'Tulguma' war strategy and artillery for the first time in this war. The huge army of Ibrahim Lodi could not stand against the skilled military leadership of Babar.

question: Who was the chief military officer of 'Pargana' during the Sultanate period who maintained law and order?
solution: The structure of administration was such that the military and revenue departments kept an eye on each other. The main function of Shikdar was to prevent rebellions and maintain peace.

question: Who is the author of 'Tarikh-e-Firozshahi' and 'Fatawa-e-Jahandari'?
solution: Ziauddin Barani has written the history of the first six years of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. He was an eyewitness to the market reforms of Alauddin Khilji.

question: Into which two categories did Iltutmish divide 'Iqta'?
solution: Holders of larger iqta were called 'Mukti' or 'Wali', who had administrative powers. Holders of small iqtas could only collect revenue from there, they had no administrative powers.

question: Which title was given by Firoz Shah Tughlaq to the ruler of Bengal after defeating Haji Ilyas?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq failed to completely merge Bengal with Delhi. He realized that it was difficult to rule so far away from Delhi, so he made a treaty.

question: Which metal was used by Firoz Shah Tughlaq to erect the Ashoka Pillar in 'Firoz Shah Kotla'?
solution: This work of Firoz Shah Tughlaq is an early example of archaeological conservation. He also got an inscription installed near the pillar (which is now destroyed).

question: For what purpose was 'Gaz-e-Sikandari' used?
solution: Sikandar Lodi greatly organized the administration. He removed tax on food grains so that prices remained low. He is considered to be the most powerful Sultan of the Lodi dynasty.

question: Which dynasty was established in Delhi after the invasion of Taimur during the time of 'Naseeruddin Mahmood'?
solution: The Syed dynasty ruled until 1451. The rulers of this dynasty never took the title of Sultan, except the last rulers. They claimed to be descendants of the Prophet.

question: After the 'First Battle of Panipat' (1526), ​​Babur visited the tomb of which Sultan of Delhi and paid his respects?
solution: Ibrahim Lodi's tomb is still situated in the grounds of Panipat. It is a memorial to the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who was martyred while fighting in the war.

question: What was the chief assistant officer of 'Diwan-e-Wizarat' called during the Sultanate period?
solution: The post of Vizier was so busy that he needed many assistants. The Naib Vizir was often a loyal relative of the Sultan or an experienced official.

question: Along with 'Qutub Minar', which other monument was repaired by Sikandar Lodi?
solution: Sikandar Lodi was interested in architecture, but he laid more emphasis on the restoration of old buildings rather than new buildings. He wanted the pride of Delhi to remain intact.

question: What was 'Khums' tax?
options: Share of the goods looted in war: According to Islamic law, 1/5 share of the loot belonged to the Sultan and 4/5 share to the soldiers.
solution: Alauddin Khilji reversed the rule and kept 4/5 of the loot for himself and gave 1/5 to the soldiers. Firoz Tughlaq again fixed 1/5 for the Sultan as per Sharia.

question: 'Lajjat-e-Sikandarshahi' is a famous book based on which subject which was written during the period of Sikandar Lodi?
solution: During the time of Sikandar Lodi, coordination of Hindu and Muslim cultures was seen in the field of music. This treatise is considered to be the first important work on Indian music written in Persian.

question: Which Hindu Shahi capital near Peshawar was attacked by Mahmud Ghaznavi in ​​999 AD?
solution: Mahmud Ghaznavi attacked Wahind (Udbhandpur), located at the gateway to India, to clear the way for plunder into the interior parts of India. This was one of his early successful campaigns.

question: Which Sultan established 'Diwan-e-Isthakaq' (Pension Department)?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq did many works for public welfare. He also created 'Diwan-e-Khairat' to help widows and orphans.

question: Why did Alauddin Khilji ban 'Alcohol'?
options: To prevent social gatherings and conspiracies among the nobles, the nobles used to meet together in liquor parties and make plans against the Sultan.
There was a shortage of wine
solution: Along with liquor, Alauddin also made the Sultan's permission mandatory for gambling and mutual marriages of nobles. He punished drug addicts by throwing them into a 'blind well'.

question: During the Sultanate period, was 'Ariz-e-Mumalik', the head of 'Diwan-e-Arz' department, the chief commander of the army after the Sultan?
options: Yes, he was the master of the entire army.
He only looked after the horses.
No, he was only the head of recruitment and logistics
solution: The duty of the Ariz was to record the appearance of the soldiers, brand the horses and arrange provisions (food and drink) during war. He helped the Sultan in military strategy.

question: Which was the first Afghan dynasty to rule the Delhi Sultanate?
solution: The governance system of Lodi rulers was different from that of the Turks. He considered the Sultan as 'first among equals' rather than an autocratic ruler. Bahlol Lodi used to sit on the carpet with his nobles.

question: Which additional grain did Alauddin Khilji take from the farmers of the 'Doab' region along with the tax?
options: Did not take any extra grain
solution: Alauddin wanted that there should never be any shortage of grains in Delhi. He had filled the government warehouses with grains so much that the prices did not rise even during the famine.

question: For what purpose did Sikandar Lodi build 'Moth ki Masjid'?
options: A place of prayer for the general public
solution: Moth Ki Masjid is called 'Dal Ki Masjid' because the entire cost of its construction was met from the income of several years of the crop obtained by sowing just one handful of 'Moth' (lentil) grains. This was a symbol of the honesty of the minister.

question: What was the name of the father of Mahmud Ghaznavi who laid the foundation of the independent Ottoman state in Ghazni?
solution: It was Subuktagin who defeated King Jaipal for the first time. Mahmud carried forward his father's legacy and made Ghazni the superpower of Central Asia.

question: After the withdrawal of 'token currency', coins of which metal were again mainly introduced by Mohammad Bin Tughlaq?
solution: During the time of MBT, gold coins were called 'Dinar'. He paid great attention to the weight and purity of the coins, hence he is also called the “Prince of Moneyers”.

question: What was the real name of Alauddin Khilji?
solution: Alauddin Khilji became Sultan by killing his uncle and father-in-law Jalaluddin Khilji. He got Jalaluddin killed in Kada (Allahabad). He is famous in history for his market control reforms.

question: Who was the chief administrative officer at the 'Pargana' level during the Sultanate period?
solution: The units of administration were: Iqta (province) -> Shiq (district) -> Pargana (tehsil) -> Village. Pargana was a group of many villages and here along with Amil there was also 'Kanungo'.

question: Which system was started by Alauddin Khilji by ending the 'Iqta' system?
solution: Alauddin was the first Sultan of Delhi to give cash salary. A cavalry soldier (Murattab) was given 234 tankas per year. If he had two horses, he would get an additional 78 tankas.

question: Who was the ruler of Delhi Sultanate who got 'Satyamev Jayate' and 'Hindu scriptures' translated into Persian?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq got the texts of astronomy and philosophy translated under the name 'Dalayl-e-Firozshahi'. He was a staunch Sultan but he was interested in knowledge and architecture.

question: In which year did Mahmud Ghaznavi's famous attack on Somnath temple take place?
solution: The invasion of Somnath was the most devastating attack of Mahmud Ghaznavi. At that time the ruler of Gujarat was Bhimdev I. Ghaznavi looted the immense wealth of the temple and broke the Shivalinga.

question: Who became the Sultan after the death of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
solution: The reign of Mohammad bin Tughlaq is known for his bold but failed plans. At that time the Delhi Sultanate had reached its maximum geographical expansion.

question: Which idea did Sikandar Lodi give prominence to in his poems 'Gulrukhi'?
solution: Sikandar Lodi's dual personality is famous in history - on one hand he was a fanatic ruler who broke the idols of Jwalamukhi temple, and on the other hand he was a sensitive Persian poet.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Tarikh-e-Mubarakshahi' which throws light on the history of the Syed dynasty?
solution: This is the only contemporary reliable source of information about the Syed dynasty. The Syed rulers ruled the Delhi Sultanate for 37 years.

question: Which Sultan waived off 'Sondhar' agricultural loans?
solution: To win the hearts of the farmers, Firoz Shah Tughlaq publicly burnt the documents in which the loan accounts were written. This brought great relief to the farmers.

question: Mahmud Ghaznavi's last military campaign (1027 AD) was against whom?
options: The campaign against the Chandela king
solution: Ghaznavi's 17th and final invasion was against the Jats and Khokhars living along the banks of the Indus River. He died in Ghazni in 1030 AD.

question: What was the nickname of the poems written by Sikandar Lodi?
solution: Sikandar Lodi was a staunch ruler. He broke the idols of the Jwalamukhi temple and gave the meat to butchers for weighing. He re-imposed Jaziya and pilgrimage tax on Hindus.

question: What was 'Dar-ul-Shifa' which was established in Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq also got Ayurvedic texts translated into Persian to promote medical science. He himself was interested in the knowledge of herbs.

question: What was 'Khidmati' during the Sultanate period?
options: Tax paid by the defeated kings
solution: The service tax showed that the local king accepted the subordination of the Sultan. If any king refused to serve, the Sultan would attack him.

question: Which practice was banned by Sikandar Lodi on the festival of 'Muharram'?
options: Taking out Tajiya and women visiting tombs
solution: Sikandar Lodi tried to remove those evils prevalent in the Muslim society which according to him were against the purity of Islam. He also banned the worship of pirs and saints.

question: What was the department of 'Diwan-e-Arz' related to during the Sultanate period?
solution: The head of the military department was called 'Ariz-e-Mumalik'. He managed the recruitment, supervision and logistics of troops, but was not the commander-in-chief (Sultan).

question: Through whom did 'Amil', the chief revenue officer of 'Pargana', connect with the farmers?
solution: The autonomy of the villages remained. The Sultan was only concerned with revenue. The role of Patwari and Muqaddam was most important in the internal affairs of the village.

question: For whom did Sikandar Lodi give the message of 'love' in 'Gulrukhi'?
solution: Sikandar Lodi's literary contribution is completely different from his political image. He was a poet with a sensitive heart who used to worship God in solitude.

question: Mohammad Bin Tughlaq used 'token currency' by issuing coins of which metal?
solution: Inspired by Kublai Khan of China and Gekhatu Khan of Iran, MBT did this experiment. But he could not control the government mint, due to which counterfeit coins flooded the market.

question: What was the rate of interest on loans (Sondhar) given to farmers under the 'Dewan-e-Amir-Kohi' department?
solution: Sultan Mbiti wanted the farmers to be happy so that the revenue of the state would increase. However, his officials also turned this selfless plan into a means of plunder.

question: In which year did Mohammad Bin Tughlaq shift the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
solution: During the transfer of the capital, the Sultan ordered the complete evacuation of Delhi. The elderly and the sick were also dragged away, which spread hatred towards the Sultan among the general public.

question: Apart from taxes, which 'forced' labor did Alauddin Khilji order the farmers of 'Doab' to do?
options: He did not impose any forced labor but only took high wages.
solution: Alauddin Khilji was a practical ruler. He did not promote forced labor because he wanted farmers to concentrate only on farming so that the supply of grains would not stop.

question: Which duty was removed by Sikandar Lodi on 'grains' so that the general public got relief?
solution: Sikandar Lodi was an efficient administrator. He built inns, bridges and roads. In his time the justice system was very strict and the Sultan himself kept every small news through spies.

question: What punishment did Alauddin Khilji decide for the shopkeepers who broke the rules of 'market control'?
options: Cutting flesh from the body equal to less weighed grain
solution: Alauddin's punishments were very violent and scary. According to Barani, even children used to go to the market and buy goods without bargaining because the shopkeepers did not dare to cheat.

question: Why did Alauddin Khilji implement the 'Daag' and 'Huliya' system?
options: To prevent corruption and fraud in the army, soldiers used to bring the same horse for inspection again and again or send inferior soldiers.
It was mandatory for all soldiers to recognize Rajput soldiers.
solution: Under the Hulia system, a soldier's physical details (e.g. scars, height) were recorded. In the Daag tradition, the royal seal was put on the horse. This created a strong and transparent standing army.

question: What was the value of the copper coins introduced by Mohammad Bin Tughlaq as 'token currency'?
options: Gold was very valuable, copper could not be equal to it.
solution: This scheme of MBT was similar to modern paper currency. But the flood of counterfeit coins made it a currency based on the intrinsic value of the metal, causing huge losses to the state.

question: Who was the third important officer in the 'Diwan-e-Wizarat' department apart from 'Mushrif' and 'Mustaufi'?
solution: The treasurer kept track of how much money came into the treasury and how much went out. The khazin could not take out even a single coin without the permission of the vizier.

question: What was the main difference between 'Mushrif-e-Mumalik' and 'Mustaufi-e-Mumalik'?
options: Mushrif used to collect taxes and Mustafi kept it in the treasury.
Mushrif was the head of the army and Mustafi was the head of the market.
Both were two names of the same department.
Mushrif kept track of the income and Mustafi checked the expenses
solution: Both these officers worked under the Wazir. The finances of the Sultanate depended on the balance between these two so that embezzlement could not occur.

question: Which second war did 'Ibrahim Lodi' fight after the Battle of Khatauli (1517) to take revenge from Rana Sanga?
solution: Ibrahim Lodi had handed over the leadership of his army to his generals, but the Lodi army could not stand against the war policy of Rana Sanga. These defeats reduced the confidence of Ibrahim's nobles in him.

question: By what name did Bahlol Lodi start calling 'Iqta'?
solution: Bahlol Lodi strengthened the Iqtadari again because he needed the support of the Afghan chieftains. He gave complete freedom to the Iqtadars in their areas.

question: Why did Iltutmish stop the 'Iqta' system from being hereditary?
options: To keep the power of the Sultan strong
On the orders of the Caliph
solution: Iltutmish used to transfer Iqtadars frequently. It was Firoz Shah Tughlaq who made Iqta hereditary, thereby weakening the Delhi Sultanate.

question: What kind of 'espionage system' was established by Balban?
options: The network of spies under Barid-e-Mumalik
solution: Balban's Barid were so powerful that if any governor spoke against the Sultan even in his own home, the Barid would inform the Sultan. The dead person was also hanged for not giving information.

question: According to Ibn Battuta, what was the 'Uluq' postal system in the Delhi Sultanate?
solution: Ibn Battuta was greatly impressed by the efficiency of the postal system. He told that the Sultan could get information from any corner of India in a very short time.

question: How many members were there in 'Turkan-e-Chihalgani' and what was their origin?
solution: The Chalisa Dal (Chalisa) was the basis of the Sultan's power. After the death of Iltutmish, this group became the king maker.

question: 'Tamur Lang' refused to declare which nobleman as 'Sultan' in Delhi and gave him only the post of 'Governor'?
solution: Khizr Khan's humility and loyalty made him the next ruler of Delhi. He never got the Khutba read in his own name, rather he remained loyal to Taimur and his son Shahrukh.

question: Why did 'Qutubuddin Aibak' not take the title of Sultan?
options: Because he considered himself the commander (malik and commander) of Ghori
The public did not like him
solution: Aibak had received the letter of freedom from slavery (Dasta Mukti Patra) from Ghiya's successor Ghiyasuddin Mahmud, but still he did not call himself Sultan.

question: Which new tax was imposed by Firoz Shah Tughlaq during his reign despite it being against 'Sharia'?
solution: Firoz Shah abolished 24 burdensome taxes (such as ghari and grazing). He collected only those taxes which were written in the Quran. The irrigation tax was the result of his economic foresight.

question: Who was the main operator of 'artillery' in Babur's victory in the 'First Battle of Panipat'?
solution: The Indian Army had never seen the sound of cannons and their devastating impact before. Due to the cannons, Ibrahim Lodi's elephants went crazy and started trampling his own army.

question: Where did his brother 'Jalal Khan', who rebelled against Ibrahim Lodi, declare his independent rule?
solution: Jalal Khan's rebellion made Ibrahim Lodi more suspicious and cruel. He lost confidence in his nobles, which shook the entire administration.

question: What was the main reason for Ghori's victory in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD)?
options: The superior cavalry and war tactics of the Turks
solution: The second battle of Tarain was the turning point of Indian history. This established Turkish rule over Delhi and Ajmer and ended the power of Prithviraj Chauhan.

question: Who made Agra the capital of Delhi Sultanate?
solution: Agra was established as a military cantonment to control Rajput rebellions. Sikandar Lodi transformed it into a trading and cultural centre.

question: What was 'Gaz-i-Sikandari'?
solution: This scale remained in use during the Mughal period until the introduction of 'Gaj-e-Ilahi' during the time of Akbar. Sikandar Lodi also got the texts of Ayurveda translated into Persian under the name 'Farhange-Sikandari'.

question: Which new right did Firoz Shah Tughlaq give to the nobles after making 'Iqta' hereditary?
options: The right to choose the new Sultan
The right to have an army
The right to give exemption in taxes was decided by the Sultan.
Right to sell and mortgage Iqtaar
solution: This policy of Firoz Shah shook the foundation of Delhi Sultanate. Iqtadars were now busy protecting their jagirs instead of being loyal to the Sultan.

question: Who was the author of 'Shahnama' who was associated with the court of Mahmud Ghaznavi?
solution: Mahmud Ghaznavi was a patron of scholars. There were great writers like Firdausi (Shahnama), Al-Biruni (Tahqiq-e-Hind) and Al-Utbi in his court. Firdausi wrote Shahnama to revive Persian pride.

question: Who were the 'Wali' or 'Muqti' during the Sultanate period?
options: The officers who dispense justice were called Qazi.
solution: The function of the Iqtadars (Muktis) was to maintain law and order and help the Sultan with his army. Alauddin Khilji had greatly reduced the power of the Iqtadars.

question: During the Sultanate period, the post of 'Khazin' came under which department?
solution: The Khazin had to be answerable to the Vizier. He used to give details of the condition of the treasury to the Sultan every evening.

question: Where did Qutubuddin Aibak make his capital?
solution: Aibak was Sultan from 1206 to 1210 AD. He was the founder of Turkish power in Indian territory but his entire time was spent in suppressing rebellions.

question: Which place was built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq for the nobles who were under the influence of 'liquor'?
options: He allowed liquor in the tavern.
He did not build any place, but imposed a complete ban on alcohol
He had exempted only the Ulemas.
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq tried to paint the public life of Delhi completely in Islamic colours. He also banned music and dance programs.

question: What was the office of 'Mustaufi-e-Mumalik' called during the Sultanate period?
solution: Through Diwan-e-Ishraf, the Sultan ensured that not a single part of the state's income was spent wrongly. Mustafi used to closely check the expenses of every department.

question: At which place did Bahlol Lodi sacrifice his life while returning from 'Gwalior'?
solution: Bahlol Lodi ruled for 38 years, the longest tenure for any Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. He is remembered for his simplicity and Afghan pride.

question: On whom did Firoz Shah Tughlaq impose a tax called 'Haq-e-Sharb'?
options: This was Alauddin's house tax on houses.
The trade tax on trade was Zakat.
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built 5 big and 30 small canals. He consulted the Ulemas whether he could carry out irrigation, and implemented it only after their permission.

question: Of which metal did Bahlol Lodi make 'Bahloli Coins'?
solution: The value of the Bahloli coin was equal to 1/40 tanka. During the Lodi period, the economy was more agriculture based and copper coins were sufficient for exchange.

question: What title was given to him by 'Minhaj-us-Siraj' during the reign of 'Razia Sultan'?
solution: Razia got "Iltutmish's daughter" written on her coins to prove her hereditary legitimacy. He attained the throne with the support of the people of Delhi.

question: Which famous Hindi poet was honored by Sikandar Lodi in his court?
solution: The Bhakti movement was at its peak during the time of Sikandar Lodi. There are many folktales prevalent about the conflict between Kabir's pure devotion and Alexander's fanaticism.

question: Where was 'Daulat Khan Lodi' the governor of during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi?
solution: Daulat Khan Lodi hoped that Babar would defeat Ibrahim and become the king of Punjab, but Babar decided to settle in India.

question: In whose memory was the city of 'Jaunpur' established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq built?
solution: Jaunpur was called 'Shiraz of the East' because it became a great center of learning and culture in the medieval period.

question: Which Iranian custom did 'Balban' implement in his court?
solution: Balban believed that "the heart of the Sultan is a reflection of God." He deployed tall Negro bodyguards in the court who stood with drawn swords.

question: Who was the 'Kotwal' of Delhi during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi who conspired against him?
solution: Ibrahim Lodi was trapped in the trap of his own people. His nobles started calling him the 'Sultan of Glass' who could break at any time.

question: Which practice was started by Alauddin Khilji to maintain the quality of 'horses'?
solution: The Daag system stopped corruption in the army. Earlier, Sardar used to bring inferior horses and get them inspected, but after getting the seal, he could not do so.

question: What was the fate of 'Karachil' campaign during the time of Mohammad Bin Tughlaq?
options: The army was destroyed due to heavy snowfall and disease.
The army rebelled and killed the Sultan
solution: The purpose of the Karachil campaign was to demonstrate its power in the Himalayan regions. Although the local king submitted, thousands of the Sultan's skilled soldiers were killed.

question: Which new officer was appointed by Alauddin Khilji to stop 'Lateral Erosion' and increase revenue?
solution: Alauddin Khilji made the revenue department (Diwan-e-Mustakharaj) so powerful that even small employees were afraid of evading revenue. He increased the salaries of muharris (clerks) so that they would not take bribes.

question: Which fort was named 'Khizrabad' by Alauddin Khilji?
solution: The incident of Jauhar of Queen Padmini took place during the conquest of Chittor. Alauddin got the fort repaired and also constructed a bridge there.

question: Mohammad Bin Tughlaq forced the people of which religion to accompany him at the time of 'transfer of the capital'?
options: People of all religions and classes
solution: The Sultan had ordered that no dog or cat should be left in Delhi. Ibn Battuta wrote that a lame man and a blind man who could not go were also forcibly taken away.

question: Who was appointed by Mohammad Ghori as the Governor of Delhi after the victory of Tarain in 1192 AD?
solution: Aibak made 'Indraprastha' near Delhi his headquarters. He had completely brought the areas of Meerut, Aligarh and Delhi under Turkish control.

question: Which Rajput dynasty had built 'Qila Rai Pithora' in Delhi?
solution: 'Qila Rai Pithora' is considered to be the first city of Delhi. It was founded by the Tomars, which later became the center of the Chauhans and then the Sultans of the Ghulam dynasty.

question: What modifications/repairs did Firoz Shah Tughlaq get done in 'Qutub Minar'?
options: A door was built near the minaret
Decreased the height of the tower
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was very interested in repairing old buildings. He also got Hauz-e-Shamsi and Hauz-e-Khas repaired.

question: Where was Mohammad Bin Tughlaq's 'Karachil Campaign' (1330) for?
options: The target for the capital of Tibet was the Himalayan region.
solution: The Karachil campaign was initially successful, but heavy rain and snowfall caused the Ottoman forces to lose their way. According to Ibn Battuta, "only 10 officers returned alive."

question: Whom did Ibrahim Lodi declare as his successor when he foresaw his defeat in the battle of 'Panipat'?
options: He did not announce it to anyone
solution: Ibrahim Lodi had no children who could take over the throne at that time. After his death there was no powerful claimant left for the Lodi dynasty.

question: Where was 'Jalaluddin Khilji' murdered?
solution: In 1296 AD, Alauddin Khilji cut off Jalaluddin's head and took it to the camp of Kada. Jalaluddin's liberal rule ended with a bloody revolution.

question: Firoz Shah Tughlaq had imposed 'Jizya' tax on Brahmins also. Which Sultan of Delhi was the one who did this?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq collected only those taxes which were approved in the Quran (Kharaj, Zakat, Jaziya and Khums). He also imposed irrigation tax (Haq-e-Sharb) because he built many big canals.

question: By whom was the city of Agra founded in 1504 AD?
solution: Sikandar Lodi was the most capable ruler of the Lodi dynasty. He introduced 'Gaz-e-Sikandari' (32 digit scale) for land measurement. He used to write poems in Persian under the pseudonym 'Gulrukhi'.

question: Which department was created by Balban to control his nobles under the policy of 'Blood and Iron'?
solution: Balban's spies were called 'Barid'. If any Barid did not give correct information to the Sultan, he was publicly hanged. Due to this, discipline and fear prevailed in the administration.

question: Which Sultan arranged for 'Sondhar' loans during the famine?
solution: The MBT spent 70 lakh tankas through 'Diwan-e-Amir-Kohi' for agricultural reform, but the officials divided this money among themselves and the scheme failed.

question: 'Hassan-un-Nizami' was the court writer of which Sultan who wrote 'Taj-ul-Ma'Asir'?
solution: Taj-ul-Ma'asir describes events from 1191 to 1217 AD. This is the most important contemporary source on Aibak's conquests.

question: When did Mohammad Bin Tughlaq introduce copper coins as 'token currency'?
solution: MBT valued these coins as 'Adli' or 'Tanka'. If he had used the royal seal (security features) to stop counterfeit coins, it might have been successful.

question: What was 'Sondhar' which was given by Mohammad bin Tughlaq?
solution: MBT made great efforts for agricultural reform. The purpose of the Sondhar loans was to promote farming so that taxes could be collected in the Doab region, but the plan failed due to drought.

question: Which new system was used by Bahlol Lodi to collect 'revenue'?
solution: Bahlol Lodi lacked a strong administrative machinery. He relied on tribal loyalty, which later led to the weakening of the Lodi dynasty.

question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi Sultanate who first organized the 'Board of Revenue' (Diwan-e-Wazarat)?
solution: Iltutmish molded the administrative structure on the Persian model. He gave clear powers to posts like Wazir, Ariz and Qazi.

question: By what name did Firoz Shah Tughlaq get the Sanskrit texts obtained from the Jwalamukhi temple translated into Persian during the 'Nagarkot' campaign?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was interested in ancient knowledge. He also built an observatory in Delhi. He spread knowledge by getting Sanskrit astronomy and philosophy texts translated into Persian.

question: What was 'Iqta'?
options: Land given in lieu of salary
solution: Iltutmish firmly implemented the Iqta system in India. Iqtadar (Mukti) collected taxes from that land and maintained his own army. Firoz Tughlaq had made it hereditary.

question: At which place did 'Tamur Lang' build a huge tower after his victory in Delhi?
options: He had built the Vijay Stambh.
He had built a tower of dead bodies
solution: This description of Timur's cruelty is one of the darkest pages of medieval history. He went back after turning Delhi into a complete graveyard.

question: What was the function of 'Barid-e-Mandi' in Alauddin Khilji's 'market system'?
solution: Alauddin adopted the policy of 'checks and balances'. Shahana ran the market and Barid kept an eye on it. Due to this the possibility of corruption was reduced to zero.

question: 'Farhange-Sikandari' translated by Sikandar Lodi is a book on which subject?
solution: Sikandar Lodi had great interest in literature and knowledge. He was a well-educated ruler who even encouraged Hindus in the administration to learn Persian.

question: Who was 'Vakil-e-Dar' during the Sultanate period?
solution: Wakil-e-Dar was a very influential post as he was closest to the Sultan. He also managed the salaries of the royal harem and palace staff.

question: Which king of Warangal (1310 AD) was defeated by 'Malik Kafur'?
solution: The conquest of Warangal was a major success of Alauddin's southern campaigns. King Prataparudra Dev accepted the suzerainty of the Sultan and promised to pay taxes every year.

question: How did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq die?
options: Due to the fall of the wooden palace, the wooden pavilion built to welcome him in Afghanpur collapsed, due to which he was crushed to death.
solution: Some historians consider it an accident, while according to Ibn Battuta and Barani it was a conspiracy hatched by Juna Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) so that he could become Sultan soon.

question: Why did Mohammad Bin Tughlaq decide to return back to Delhi from 'Daulatabad'?
options: It was very hot in the south
It was difficult to rule North India from the South
solution: In 1335 AD the Sultan ordered to go back to Delhi. Even more people died on this second long journey. This plan ruined the reputation of the Sultan.

question: 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' mosque was built in memory of which victory?
options: Turkish conquest of Delhi and North India
solution: Quwwat-ul-Islam means 'Power of Islam'. This mosque was built by demolishing 27 Hindu and Jain temples. The famous 'Iron Pillar' of the Gupta period is still safe in its courtyard.

question: 'Amir-e-Kohi' department was established by which Sultan?
solution: Mohammad bin Tughlaq distributed 'Sondhar' (loans) for agricultural reforms. However, this plan could not succeed due to corruption of officials and bad weather.

question: The Battle of Chandawar (1194 AD) was fought between Mohammad Ghori and which Rajput ruler?
solution: After the victory of Tarain, Ghori turned towards Kannauj. With the defeat of Jaichand in the battle of Chandawar, a large part of Northern India came under Turkish control. Jaichand is also remembered as a traitor in some folk tales.

question: Which African slave was appointed as 'Amir-e-Akhoor' (head of the stable) by 'Razia Sultan'?
solution: The Ottoman nobleman (Chalisa) could not tolerate that a non-Turk slave should be so close to the Sultan. He murdered Yakut and conspired to remove Razia from the throne.

question: When did Sikandar Lodi make 'Agra' city his capital?
solution: The main purpose of establishing Agra was to keep an eye on the Rajput kings of Etawah, Bayana and Gwalior. Sikandar Lodi also built a fort here which is called 'Badalgarh'.

question: How much army did Mohammad Bin Tughlaq prepare for the 'Khorasan Campaign' and then why did he disband it?
options: 370,000 soldiers; Due to changing political situation in Iran, the Sultan had given one year's cash salary advance to the soldiers, due to which the treasury was emptied.
50,000 soldiers; The path was very difficult.
solution: The dream of conquering Khorasan (Iran) was another airborne plan of the MBT. After disbanding the army, these unemployed soldiers started looting, due to which law and order in the state deteriorated.

question: For how many days did 'Taimur Lang' continue the massacre and looting in Delhi?
solution: Taimur did not differentiate between Hindus and Muslims. He also killed those Muslim Ulamas of Delhi who had begged him for mercy. He left only craftsmen and artists alive.

question: Whom did Rana Sanga defeat in the 'Battle of Khatauli' (1517)?
solution: The battle of Khatauli made the power of Rajputs supreme in North India. Ibrahim Lodi was very enraged by this defeat and was determined to take revenge from the Rajputs.

question: How many times did 'Babar' attack India during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi?
solution: Babur wrote in his memoirs that the political instability of India encouraged him to build an empire here. He called Ibrahim Lodi an "inexperienced young man".

question: Which Sultan used to write poems under the pseudonym 'Gulrukhi'?
solution: Sikandar Lodi established the city of Agra and again imposed Jaziya on Hindus. He also got the upper floor of Qutub Minar repaired.

question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi who fled the city during Taimur Lang's invasion (1398)?
solution: Taimur looted and massacred in Delhi for 15 days. He did not spare both Hindus and Muslims. Tughlaq Sultan later returned but his power was completely destroyed.

question: What type of carvings are found on the first floor of 'Qutub Minar'?
solution: Qutub Minar is made of red sandstone. The 'jharokas' (balconies) in its structure are an excellent example of the Muqarnas (Stalactite) style.

question: When did Iltutmish conquer the famous fort of 'Ranthambore'?
solution: Conquering Ranthambore was always challenging for the Sultans of Delhi. By winning it, Iltutmish established the rule of Turks in Rajasthan.

question: What punishment did Balban give to the rebellious Bengal Governor 'Tughril Khan' under the policy of 'blood and iron'?
options: After killing him, his head was sent to Delhi and his supporters were publicly hanged.
solution: This punishment of Balban was so terrible that according to Barani, "the souls of the spectators shuddered." After this, no one dared to revolt in Bengal for the next 20 years.

question: After the death of Bahlol Lodi, which of his sons became Sultan by the name of 'Sikandar Lodi'?
solution: Nizam Khan's mother was the daughter of a Hindu goldsmith, due to which some Afghan chieftains opposed him. But due to his bravery and intelligence he succeeded in becoming the Sultan.

question: Why did Alauddin Khilji create the post of 'Shahana-e-Mandi'?
options: For the royal cooks, the cooks were not related to the market.
To control the grain market, he ensured that traders did not rig prices and kept the weight correct.
solution: Alauddin appointed Malik Kabul as the first Shahana-e-Mandi. The main objective of market reforms was to provide good goods to the army at low wages.

question: What was the main objective of the establishment of 'Diwan-e-Amir-Kohi' department?
options: Increasing the salary of soldiers: Alauddin had started giving cash salary to the soldiers.
solution: MBT gave 'Takkavi' or 'Sondhar' loans to famine victims for agricultural reforms. He created an agricultural block of 60 miles under 'Diwan-i-Kohi' but it failed due to corruption.

question: The 'Token Currency' introduced by Mohammad Bin Tughlaq was made of which metal?
solution: The token currency plan failed miserably as people started minting fake coins in every home. Foreign merchants refused to accept these coins, causing trade to come to a standstill.

question: 'Sadar-e-Jahan' was the other name of which department during the Sultanate period?
solution: Sadar-e-Jahan was also called 'Sheikh-ul-Islam'. He informed the Sultan about religious laws (fatwa) and appointed all the Qazis of the state.

question: After whom did Alauddin Khilji change the name of Chittor to 'Khizrabad' after conquering it?
options: In the name of his son Khizr Khan, Khizr Khan was appointed the first Ottoman governor there.
Named after Khizr Khan, the founder of the Syed dynasty
Named after the Sultan of Ghazni
solution: The fall of Chittor in 1303 AD was a major event in Rajput history. The Rajputs continued a guerrilla war against Alauddin for several years, ultimately forcing Khizr Khan to abandon Chittor.

question: The work of 'Diwan-e-Rasalat' was most associated with religious fanaticism during the time of which Sultan?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq stopped Muslim women from visiting the shrines of saints and tortured Shia Muslims. He implemented his fanaticism through the religious department.

question: Where was the 'Battle of Bari' (1518) fought between Ibrahim Lodi and Rana Sanga?
solution: After the victory in the battle of Bari, Rana Sanga's influence reached the borders of Agra. Ibrahim Lodi's prestige fell greatly due to this defeat and there was division in his court.

question: What was the main geographical reason for the failure of 'Diwan-e-Kohi' department?
options: The land chosen was barren and unsuitable for farming
The Mongols had burnt the fields
solution: Mohammad bin Tughlaq's intentions were right but he did not check the 'ground report'. Even after spending 70 lakh tanka, not a single grain of grain was produced.

question: Which new crop did Mohammad Bin Tughlaq suggest to introduce for 'agricultural reform'?
solution: MBT wanted farmers not to grow only grains but to grow crops that could yield more revenue. He had arranged training for this through 'Amir-e-Kohi' department.

question: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi Sultanate to get 'construction of canals' done?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built long canals from Sutlej to Ghaggar and from Yamuna to Hisar. Agricultural production increased due to irrigation and Firoz also imposed an irrigation tax called 'Haq-e-Sharb'.

question: Which coin was named 'Jital' by Iltutmish?
solution: 1 silver tanka = 48 copper jitals. This coin system became the basis of the monetary economy of medieval India.

question: What was 'Sara-e-Adal' in Alauddin Khilji's market policy?
options: Market of manufactured goods and precious clothes
solution: Sara-e-Adal was an open ground near Badaun Gate. The prices of the goods here were fixed by the Sultan himself so that luxury goods could also reach the middle class.

question: During which campaign did Alauddin Khilji take 'Malik Kafur' with him?
solution: Malik Kafur was also known as 'Hazar Dinari'. He not only became Alauddin's commander but also his most trusted advisor and ultimately the Sultan's deputy (Malik Naib).

question: What was the rate of 'Kharaj' fixed by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
solution: The main objective of Firoz Shah Tughlaq was to please the Muslim subjects. For the welfare of farmers, he reduced taxes and increased irrigation facilities.

question: By whom was the Delhi Sultanate established in 1206 AD?
solution: The Delhi Sultanate was ruled by five dynasties: Ghulam, Khilji, Tughlaq, Syed and Lodi. Qutbuddin Aibak was a loyal slave of Mohammad Ghori, hence the first dynasty was called Ghulam or Mamluk dynasty.

question: Where did Mohammad Ghori launch his first attack on India in 1175 AD?
solution: Ghori's main objective was to establish the Muslim empire in India. After Multan he attacked Uttar Pradesh and then Gujarat, where he was defeated.

question: To which Sultan is the book 'Tabaqat-e-Nasiri' dedicated?
solution: It is said about Naseeruddin Mahmood that he used to sew caps and copy the Quran for his living. The real power was in the hands of his minister Balban.

question: Where was 'Madrasa-e-Firozshahi' built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq located?
options: Inside Firozshah Kotla, he had built Jama Masjid there.
Near Qutub Minar there were madrassas of Iltutmish and Alauddin.
solution: In this madrasa, not only Islamic theology but also logic and science were taught. Firoz Shah also arranged scholarships and free meals for the students.

question: Which was the longest canal among the canals built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq for 'irrigation'?
solution: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built a total of 5 big canals. The construction of canals led to the expansion of agricultural land and the Sultan also planted 1200 fruit orchards there, which brought income to the royal treasury.

question: For how long did 'Malik Kafur' hold power after the death of Alauddin Khilji?
solution: Malik Kafur's ambition became the cause of his downfall. He had Alauddin's elder sons blinded. After his death Mubarak Khilji became the Sultan.

question: What was the capital of the 'Hindu Shahi' dynasty at the time of the invasion of Mahmud Ghaznavi?
solution: The Hindu Shahi dynasty ruled the regions of Afghanistan and Punjab. Ghaznavi broke the back of this kingdom by defeating King Jaipal in 1001 AD.

question: Why is tax increase in the 'Doab' region considered the biggest mistake of Mohammad Bin Tughlaq?
options: Because the tax rate was very low the
Due to increasing taxes during times of famine and drought
Taxes were increased to please the Mongols
The farmers had a lot of money.
solution: The taxation of the Doab (1325-26) was his first major scheme. Unfortunately it did not rain that year. By the time the Sultan realized his mistake and sent relief, it was too late.

question: According to 'Tarikh-e-Mubarakshahi', which ruler of the Syed dynasty was the one who established the city of 'Mubarakabad'?
solution: It was during the time of Mubarak Shah that the famous historian Yahya bin Ahmed Sirhindi wrote his book, which is the only major source on the history of the Syed dynasty.

question: How many times did Mahmud Ghaznavi attack India?
solution: Mahmud Ghaznavi was the ruler of the Ghazni Empire in Central Asia. He attacked India 17 times between 1001 and 1027 AD to plunder the wealth of India. His most famous attack was on the Somnath temple in 1025 AD.
